The things worth knowing before you take the next step.
I’m still researching. Is it too early to talk?+
That is a good time to start. You do not need a selected visa or a property shortlist. A first conversation helps put your options, timeline and next decisions in order.
Can you help with both my visa and my home?+
Yes. We coordinate the visa questions and your housing search together, so the lease, location and arrival timeline make sense for the same move.
How will I know what I’m paying for?+
Before paid work starts, ask for a written scope and fee breakdown. Official fees, our service fee and any third-party costs should appear separately. Changes need a revised quote.
Can you guarantee a visa approval?+
No. The embassy, BOI or immigration authority makes the decision. Our role is to explain the route, organise the evidence and help you understand what remains uncertain.
Do I need to buy property to move to Thailand?+
Buying a home is not the starting point for every move. Many people begin with a rental. Visa permission and property ownership are separate questions that deserve separate checks.
What happens after I arrive?+
We can coordinate the next steps for housing and settling in, then discuss Residency Care for the renewals and reporting relevant to your status. The scope is agreed around what you need.

No. Eligibility and the provider evidence must meet the responsible embassy's current requirements.
Can I choose a school purely to obtain a visa?+
Choose a programme you genuinely intend to attend. Your application should accurately represent your purpose.
What should I ask the school or activity provider?+
Ask about recognition, the actual programme, attendance, supporting documents, total fees and cancellation terms. Confirm accepted visa evidence independently with your responsible embassy.
Is an activity-based DTV the same as an education visa?+
They are different purposes and processes. Explain the genuine study or activity you intend to undertake and compare the current accepted routes and evidence.
How should a child’s school plan be reviewed?+
Start with the intended school attendance and the institution’s supporting documents. Review the child’s education route and any parent or guardian arrangements separately.

Love the home. Understand the ownership.
Before buying a condominium in Thailand, have the title, foreign ownership conditions and transaction reviewed for the specific unit.
Talk through my plans CHOOSE A HOME AROUND YOUR LIFE
Check the ownership conditions

Foreign condominium ownership is subject to eligibility and the building's foreign ownership limit. The Condominium Act sets that limit at 49% of the total unit area. Ask for current confirmation for the building and independent review of the unit.
Prepare the payment trail
Ask your lawyer and receiving bank what evidence is required for your funding and transfer. Do this before sending money so the records support the intended registration.
Look beyond the asking price
Review transfer costs, common-area charges, maintenance, a sinking fund if applicable and ongoing management. Forecast costs separately from any hoped-for rental income.
Keep residence and ownership separate
A property purchase does not automatically grant a visa or permission to stay. Plan your residence route independently of the transaction.
